title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: 𝔊 is a profinite group, presumably Ĝ_{1,1}, a profinite completion of SL(2,Z) or a variant. It has distinguished torsion elements ρ (order 3 or 6) and σ (order 2 or 4), modelled on the two elliptic points j=0 and j=1728 of M_{1,1}. B_{ρ,σ} is the group of pairs (u,μ), with u ∈ Aut(𝔊) and μ ∈ Ẑ^×, such that u sends ρ and σ to conjugates of ρ^μ and σ^μ. This is the 'cyclotomic' condition on torsion classes. L_0 ⊂ 𝔊 is a normal subgroup stable under B, mapped into B by l ↦ (int(l),1). It is assumed to meet the centre trivially (20). Then Γ_{ρ,σ} = B/L_0 with character χ_Γ: Γ → Ẑ^× (23–25).

On this page:
(26) Compose χ_Γ with the two sign characters ε_2, ε_3: Ẑ^× → ±1. These are reduction mod 4 and mod 3, i.e. (Z/4)^× = ±1 and (Z/3)^× = ±1. Arithmetically they are the characters of Q(i) and Q(√−3).
(27) Their kernels Γ' = Ker(ε_3∘χ) and Γ'' = Ker(ε_2∘χ) are index-2 subgroups. Γ' is the part fixing the class of ρ, since ρ^μ ~ ρ when μ ≡ 1 mod 3. Γ'' is the part fixing the class of σ, since μ ≡ 1 mod 4.
(28)–(29) Form the semidirect product B ⋉ 𝔊, with B acting on 𝔊 through u. Embed L_0 antidiagonally by l ↦ (i(l), l^{-1}); the image is normal. Set G_{ρ,σ} = (B ⋉ 𝔊)/L_0.
(30) This is the standard pushout square L_0 → 𝔊, L_0 → B into G.
Kernel check: Ker(𝔊 → G) = {l ∈ L_0 : int(l) = 1} = L_0 ∩ Z(𝔊), which is trivial by (20).
(31) Hence a morphism of extensions 1→L_0→B→Γ→1 to 1→𝔊→G→Γ→1, i.e. the pushout of the first extension along L_0 ⊂ 𝔊. There is a character χ_G = χ_Γ∘δ_G.

Purpose: build a 'universal arithmetic fundamental group' G_{ρ,σ}, an extension of the GT-like group Γ_{ρ,σ} by 𝔊, playing the role of π_1(M_{1,1,Q}) ↠ Gal(Q̄/Q). The next page uses it to show that the centralizers of ρ and σ in G surject onto Γ' and Γ''. These are the analogues of the decomposition/stabilizer groups at j=0 (field Q(√−3)) and j=1728 (field Q(i)), i.e. 'Galois sections' attached to the CM orbifold points, defined purely combinatorially.
errors: No mathematical error on this page; the kernel computation Ker(𝔊→G) ≅ L_0 ∩ Centre(𝔊) is correct.
The bottom row of (31) is also surjective onto Γ; the trailing '→1' is simply omitted.
Implicit hypotheses: L_0 must be normal in 𝔊 and stable under the u's for (B ⋉ 𝔊)/L_0 to make sense; this was established on the previous page via (21).
The identification '≃ S_0 G_{ρ,σ}' under (28) is unclear and may be a reading error or an aside.

ideas.what: Sign characters ε_2, ε_3 (mod 4, mod 3) of Ẑ^× composed with the cyclotomic-type character; index-2 subgroups fixing the conjugacy classes of the order-4 and order-6 torsion elements
ideas.modern_name: Cyclotomic action on torsion conjugacy classes of Ĝ_{1,1}; fields Q(i), Q(√−3) of the CM points j=1728, j=0
ideas.usually_credited_to: Arithmetic of M_{1,1} (classical); for GT-type groups: Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (1997), Collas and Collas–Maugeais (2010s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions Ĝ_{1,1} and the (2,3) structure but not this construction

ideas.what: Extension G = (B ⋉ 𝔊)/L_0 obtained by pushing out 1→L_0→B→Γ→1 along L_0 ⊂ 𝔊, using trivial centre
ideas.modern_name: Pushout of group extensions / extension induced by an outer action with centreless kernel
ideas.where_published: Standard; similar constructions appear throughout SGA1-style fundamental group theory

ideas.what: Universal 'arithmetic fundamental group' of M_{1,1} defined from a GT-like automorphism group Γ_{ρ,σ} of 𝔊, used to locate decomposition-type subgroups (centralizers of ρ and σ) over Γ', Γ''
ideas.modern_name: GT-type group for M_{1,1} and its action on stack inertia / elliptic points

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines, for Ĝ_{1,1}, a combinatorial Galois-type group Γ_{ρ,σ}. It is cut out by requiring automorphisms to send the torsion generators ρ, σ to conjugates of their μ-th powers. He splits it by the mod-3 and mod-4 sign characters to get the analogues of Gal(Q̄/Q(√−3)) and Gal(Q̄/Q(i)), i.e. the stabilizers of the elliptic points. This anticipates the later 'cyclotomic condition on torsion' studied by Collas and Collas–Maugeais and the GT_{1,1}-type refinements of Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early, explicit formulation of the decomposition groups at the CM orbifold points inside a purely group-theoretic GT-like setting. It may be of historical interest for crediting the 'inertia/torsion' approach to GT and M_{1,1}.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is routine extension-theoretic bookkeeping. Its interest is contextual: a Grothendieck-defined GT-like group for M_{1,1}, with explicit Q(i)/Q(√−3) index-2 subgroups tied to the elliptic points. This foreshadows 1990s–2010s work, but the ideas are natural and largely rediscovered.
transcription_corrections: Heading: 'Considérons les homomorphismes composés' (the 'Notons' crossed out) appears right.
(28): the underbrace reads '(1/2 direct)', i.e. semi-direct product B_{ρ,σ} ⋉ 𝔊.
(29): the target should be B_{ρ,σ}·𝔊 (the semidirect product), not 'B'_{ρ,σ}·G_{ρ,σ}'. The map is ℓ ↦ i_{L_0,B}(ℓ)·ℓ^{-1}; 'i_{-1}' is a misreading.
The crossed-out phrase before (31) is illegible; it is likely a false start ('un tout droit' is doubtful).
The bracket under (31) indicates χ_G: G_{ρ,σ} → Ẑ^× factoring through χ_Γ.
